newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50 -dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50 -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen mostly steady, instances $0.50 per cwt higher on lighter hog marketings, dealers and packer buyers said.

Marketings began tapering on Wednesday, with interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts coming in at 106,000 head, below the estimate of 110,000, USDA reported. Total receipts Monday and Tuesday were 13,000 head over estimate at 223,000 USDA statistics showed.
Interior receipts on Thursday were estimated at 100,000 head, compared with 111,000 last week and 103,000 last year.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants on Friday were seen unchanged from Thursday at $57.00, dealers and packer buyers there said.
Illinois top prices at the plant were expected steady at $56.00, but could firm if marketings are tight or if demand for weekend inventories becomes competitive.
Indiana/Ohio plant prices were seen steady to $0.50 higher, with a top ranging $56.50 to $57.00.
Cash hog prices also could be underpinned by outlooks for pork values to start trending higher, some sources noted.

Fresh loins at midday were quoted steady, USDA said. Also, pork bellies were $1.00 to $2.00 per cwt higher and lean trimmings were $1.00 to $2.00 lower, USDA said in its central U.S. carlot pork report. There were 25.5 loads of pork cuts and 17.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold.
